title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 123
paragraphs: Xerxes's fleet, cutting across from the headland of Ampelos to that of Canastraeum — which juts farthest into the sea of all Pallene — took on contingents of ships and men from Potidaea, Aphytis, Neapolis, Aege, Therambus, Scione, Mende, and Sane, for these are the cities that occupy the region now called Pallene, once called Phlegra. Sailing along the coast of this country also, the fleet continued on its course toward the place already mentioned, taking up contingents from the cities that come next after Pallene and border the Thermaic gulf; their names are: Lipaxus, Combreia, Lisae, Gigonus, Campsa, Smila, and Aeneia. The region in which these cities stand is called Crossaea to this very day. Sailing from Aeneia, with whose name I end the list, the fleet came straight into the Thermaic gulf and into the region of Mygdonia, and so arrived at the aforesaid Therma and at the cities of Sindus and Chalestra on the river Axius. This river is the boundary between Mygdonia and Bottiaea, the narrow coastal strip of which is occupied by the cities of Ichnae and Pella.
